Students will be able to demonstrate an understanding of the core theory, hardware, and installation of piping systems including rigid steel, copper, PVC, tubing, and flexible hose.

programs.title: Psychology
outcomes: Students will be able to identify various research methods used to study behavior and mental process.
Students will be able to identify the basic structures of the brain and nervous system.
Students will be able to apply psychological concepts and theories to everyday situations.
Students will be able to identify and apply behavior modification techniques.
Students will be able to identify the major components in a case study and how to use case studies as references when writing a research paper.

programs.title: Public Health
outcomes: Student will be able to apply a multi-dimensional approach to health that incorporates the study of social, behavioral, and physiological sciences.
Student will be able to analyze the social determinants of health and strategies for eliminating disease, illness, and health disparities among diverse populations.
Student will be able to demonstrate behavior-changing techniques to maximize personal health and community health.

Student will be able to develop preliminary skills to serve as effective advocates for community health, public health, and structural change regarding the impact of environment, socioeconomics, politics, and culture as they impact health systems.

programs.title: Sociology
outcomes: Students will be able to apply and demonstrate sociological literacy underscoring the centrality of race, class, and gender in society including multicultural, cross-cultural, and cross-national content in sociological analysis.
Students will be able to apply and demonstrate higher order critical thinking skills using major concepts and theoretical perspectives in sociological analysis through written and oral communication.

Students will be able to apply and demonstrate an empirical base of sociology across several methodologies, posing sociological questions, developing theoretical explanations, and using primary and secondary data as supporting evidence.

programs.title: Transfer studies - Cal GETC
programs.award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 30S/45Q to fewer than 60S/90Q units
outcomes: Students will be able to demonstrate critical thinking through literary works and written compositions.
Students will be able to utilize quantitative analysis and have the ability to use and criticize quantitative arguments.
Students will be able to analyze works of philosophical, historical, literary, aesthetic and cultural importance.
Students will be able to examine social and behavioral perspectives in their contemporary, historical, and geographical settings.
Students will be able to comprehend physical and biological concepts, their limitations, and the power of scientific inquiry.

programs.title: User Experience (UX) Design (COA)
programs.award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 16S/24Q to fewer than 30S/45Q units
outcomes: Students will be able to follow the design process to create and refine user-centered designs using user experience design concepts and principles.
Students will be able to utilize industry-standard applications and techniques to create low-, mid-, and high-fidelity prototypes.
Students will be able to provide input on design usability by citing various usability and accessibility standards and principles.
Students will be able to identify and explain design concerns with regard to basic HTML and CSS programming limitations.
